solution.explanation: C = S N(d₁) − K e^{−rT} N(d₂), and P = K e^{−rT} N(−d₂) − S N(−d₁). Check with put–call parity: C − P = S − K e^{−rT}. Interpretation: N(d₂) is the risk-neutral probability of finishing in the money, and N(d₁) the call's delta. A quick sanity number: the at-the-money price ≈ 0.4·S·σ√T when r ≈ 0 (100, 100, T = 1, σ = 0.2 gives ≈ 8).
